prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which established the incretin axis as a therapeutic target in type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I keep a single prize part, B006, with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Rereading the full first round, the disagreement is not about merit or maturity: all six of us ranked it first and nobody questions decades of independent confirmation or the randomized outcome evidence in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. The disagreement is about what the prize rewards. A Physiology or Medicine prize is for a discovery that changes the field, and here the discovery is the biology of the hormone: Holst on GLP-1 as the principal incretin and its actions in humans, Mojsov on the identification and synthesis of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, and Drucker on receptor biology, tissue actions and the translational concept. Without the active form the physiology could not be interpreted or exploited, and without the physiology there is nothing for analogue engineering to improve. Four of six members now hold this trio, including the chair, who moved to it after round 1, and I find that move scientifically reasoned and not a head count.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point and the chair is right to keep it open. Habener is outside the supplied names and is cited on both sides as part of the active-peptide record, and Mojsov's priority is described as contested; I cannot settle it from the ballots, and I rely on recalled history, not on documents. Leaving out Knudsen means the citation honours the discovery but not the acylated, long-acting analogues that produced liraglutide and semaglutide, so it can be read as too academic. Long-term safety data are still accumulating. The alternative reading, a prize framed as physiology plus therapy development, is coherent but would need a different citation and credit logic, and then B004 and B040 would have to be judged by the same principle.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius keeps Drucker, Holst and Knudsen and argues that a prize crediting both the science and the medicine fits the Physiology or Medicine mandate, while granting that crediting an industrial step stretches the prize toward pharmaceutical development.
responses.response: I accept that the mandate includes medicine and that Knudsen's work was decisive for the drug class. But you also concede that the field is still moving and that the drug-design chapter is not settled. That is the argument for resting the prize on the stable core, the physiology and the active peptide, which will not be revised by new agents or safety findings. Knudsen's contribution is real, but it builds on that core, and the citation can say so by referring to the therapeutic target it created. I do not see a way to hold both Mojsov and Knudsen within three names without dropping Holst or Drucker, and neither of them can be dropped.

responses.point: El-Manira holds Knudsen on the grounds that her albumin-binding acylation made the class usable, but also writes that he has not resolved whether physiology, peptide chemistry and drug engineering are one achievement or several, and that Mojsov's work is a decisive early step.
responses.response: I think your own case against is close to my answer. If physiology, peptide chemistry and drug engineering are really three kinds of work, a three-name cap cannot honour them all as one achievement, and the discovery end is the one that defines the field. You also call Mojsov's identification of the active form decisive. If we agree on that, then taking her out in favour of the third link in the chain reverses the logic of the discovery. I would take the two-part route only if the committee wants a separate therapy part, and the three-person cap makes that costly.

responses.point: The chair moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov in round 1, and asks in his summary whether a second part is possible when B006 already uses three names.
responses.response: Thank you for explaining the move. I agree that the citation can acknowledge analogue engineering without crediting it by name, and I have kept my wording so that it refers to the active form and the therapeutic target. On a second part, with B006 at three names, any added part forces the drop of a GLP-1 laureate, and I do not think the scientific case for B039 or any other candidate is strong enough to justify cutting Holst, Drucker or Mojsov. The answer on B037 is different, since I disclose below that I have co-authored with you, and I would follow committee guidance on that if it became a leading option.

responses.point: Linnarsson favours the physiology-centred trio and in round 1 raised that if the committee judged drug development inseparable from the benefit to humankind, the physiology-only configuration would be too academic.
responses.response: This is the right test and I have applied it. My answer is that the benefit to humankind rests on the identity and action of the peptide, and that the translation depended on knowledge that was independently established. I agree with your wish to say openly what the citation does not cover, and my text says discoveries of the physiology and the active form. I would add that, if documents showed that Mojsov's priority was materially weaker than described, I would reconsider the third name, and I would then lean to Knudsen over leaving the seat to Habener, who is not among the supplied names.

uncertainties: Mojsov versus Habener priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide cannot be resolved from the material before the committee; if it were shown to be materially weaker than described, my third name would be reopened.
Whether the committee will accept a citation that acknowledges the therapeutic consequence without crediting acylated analogue engineering by name.
Whether a second prize part is warranted given that it would force the removal of a GLP-1 laureate; I currently judge that it is not.
Long-term safety and outcome data for the drug class are still accumulating.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure: I have a documented nuclear-receptor collaboration with Ronald Evans, work with Johan Ericson, about twenty co-authored works with the chair Per Svenningsson (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy) and one 2009 paper with Abdel El-Manira. None involves B006 or its credited names. I would follow committee guidance on recusal if a neuroscience candidate such as B037 became the leading choice, since the chair has raised the same point and I am a co-author of the work in that area with him.
